title: Dashboards: ship overload protection dashboard + initial alert rules aligned to SLOs
creator: Aisha Bello
description:
Goal
Ship a Grafana dashboard + initial alert rules that make overload protection observable and SLO-aligned for Hosted API. The key requirement is to clearly distinguish:
- expected/intentional load shedding ("overload-protected" errors) vs
- internal platform failures (unexpected 5xx/timeouts)

Scope
1) Dashboard (Grafana)
- Overview: current overload posture by region/model/tier
- Drilldowns for gateway admission, routing/breaker state, runtime queues
- Error taxonomy breakdown (Redwood overload reason codes + HTTP mapping)
- SLO alignment panels (error budget burn for internal failures only)

2) Alert rules (initial)
- Paging alerts for internal failure signals and control plane health
- Non-paging/noise-controlled alerts for sustained shedding / breaker-open states
- Guard against flapping: require sustained window + cooldown-friendly thresholds

Non-goals
- Perfect thresholds on day 1 (we expect ENG-4840 to tune after canary)
- Customer-facing console surfaces (tracked separately)

References / specs
- Confluence: overload dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/overload-protection-dashboards.json
- Confluence: SLO & error budget policy update: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-overload-slos-and-error-budget-policy.json
- Confluence: metric standards + cardinality guidance: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/standard-metrics-for-load-shedding-and-breakers.json
- Drive: metric label/cardinality review notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/metric-names-cardinality-review-overload.json
- Related PRs:
  - Grafana + alerts PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-611.json
  - SLO toolkit accounting split: sources/github/slo-toolkit/pr-204.json

Dashboard requirements (panels)
A) Overload posture (top)
- Requests: RPS, concurrency, in-flight, by region + route/model
- Admission decisions (gateway): admitted vs shed-at-edge; stacked by tier (free/pro/enterprise) and streaming vs non-streaming
- Shed rate over time: % of requests returning overload-protected responses

B) Circuit breaker state (routing)
- Breaker state count (closed/open/half-open) by (region, model, tier)
- Breaker transitions per minute (to detect flapping)
- Breaker open reason / dominant input signal (e.g., queue depth, GPU saturation, control plane latency)

C) Runtime / GPU pool saturation
- Queue depth (bounded queue): current + p95
- Queue wait time distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- Prefill vs decode shed points: counts + reasons
- Memory pressure / KV cache guardrails: trigger rate + correlation with latency collapse

D) Customer-facing errors
- HTTP status distribution (2xx/4xx/5xx) with separate line for overload-protected (429/503) vs internal 5xx
- Redwood overload reason code breakdown (top N) by model + region
- Retry-After distribution (p50/p95) for overload responses (to validate guidance)
- Streaming: disconnect/error rate correlated with overload signals

E) SLO alignment
- Error budget burn panels:
  - Internal failures only (unexpected 5xx, timeouts, gateway/routing/runtime errors not mapped to overload)
  - Overload-protected responses tracked separately (for visibility, not paging)
- Tail latency panels (p95/p99) with overlay of shed rate (ensure shedding prevents tail collapse)

Cardinality constraints (must-have)
- No per-tenant labels in metrics/panels/alerts.
- Allowed grouping labels for dashboards: region, tier, model (or model_family where available), route_template, endpoint (chat/completions/embeddings), streaming.
- For alerts: avoid high-cardinality dimensions; prefer region + service-level aggregates, with a linked dashboard for drilldown.

Initial alert rules (proposed)
1) Paging (oncall)
- Control plane / routing health:
  - routing p99 latency > threshold for 10m (service-level)
  - breaker store / eval API error rate > threshold for 10m
- Runtime health:
  - internal runtime 5xx (non-overload) > threshold for 5m
  - OOM / crashloop signals > threshold
- SLO burn:
  - fast burn for internal failure SLO (e.g., > 2% budget in 1h) -> page

2) Non-paging / ticketing / slack notification
- Sustained shedding:
  - overload-protected response rate > threshold for 15m (notify #eng-sre + #eng-platform)
- Breaker stuck open:
  - breaker open > X% for 30m in any region/model_family (notify + create follow-up)
- Flapping watch:
  - breaker transition rate > threshold for 15m (notify; do not page)

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard exists in Grafana under "Hosted API > Overload Protection" and is linked from the SRE runbook.
- Dashboards render with bounded cardinality and do not time out under 7d lookback.
- Alert rules deployed via observability-pack and connected to oncall routing.
- Alerts follow SLO policy: load shedding should not page as an internal failure by default.
- During canary (ENG-4834), the dashboard supports answering: "Are we shedding? Why? Where? Is tail latency improving? Are internal failures down?"

Rollout plan
- Ship dashboard + alerts disabled-by-default in prod, enable notifications in canary region first.
- After 1 week of canary data, open ENG-4840 to tune thresholds + reduce noise.

Notes / open questions
- If we don’t yet have model_family, use model as a dashboard dimension but cap top-N and strongly prefer region/tier/route_template aggregates.
- Retry-After panel depends on gateway emitting header consistently (ENG-4823/ENG-4822).

Owner(s)
- Assignee: Sergio Costa (dashboards + alert rules)
- Partner: Aisha Bello (SLO alignment + oncall routing)
activity: 2025-12-02 (Aisha Bello): Created ticket. Align dashboards/alerts with new overload error taxonomy + SLO accounting split (overload-protected vs internal).
2025-12-05 (Sergio Costa): Drafted dashboard layout based on Confluence spec. Flagged metric label risks (tenant_id, raw model names) and asked for model_family label plan.
2025-12-09 (Allison Grant): Observability review: restrict alert dimensions; dashboards can drill down by model but alerts must be service-level + region only. Linked cardinality review notes.
2025-12-12 (Sergio Costa): Implemented initial dashboard JSON + alert rules in observability-pack PR-611. Added panels for breaker transitions and shed rate overlay on p99 latency.
2025-12-16 (Aisha Bello): SLO policy check: confirmed overload-protected errors excluded from internal failure SLO; added burn-rate alert wired to new SLO toolkit outputs (PR-204).
2025-12-19 (Christine Wong): Requested an additional panel: breaker open reason / dominant signal to debug flapping vs true capacity exhaustion.
2026-01-06 (Sergio Costa): Enabled alerts in us-east canary only. Noted expected behavior: sustained shedding posts to #eng-sre but does not page. Verified dashboard load time < 3s on 24h view.

2026-01-09 (Tomáš Novák): Canary validation: during synthetic spike, shed rate increased and p99 stabilized; internal 5xx stayed flat. Requested tuning task for thresholds after one week (tracked in ENG-4840).
2026-01-15 (Sergio Costa): Merged PR-611; dashboard live globally, alerts enabled per rollout plan. Added runbook linkback and confirmed oncall routing.
